title: Louis Armstrong's advice about saving his lips
summary: Armstrong told him to ease off overblowing; Hawkins describes his lip trouble.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: I remember Louis Armstrong come in there once. And after I finished the Savoy Ballroom, he carried me to, I think it was Brickwood, to sit down and talk to me about saving my lips, not overblowing. He said you may need those in the years that are coming. He said now, you made your point. Now, take it a little easy so you can have those for years to come. He said, he had some trouble with his once. He had to have some meat grafted on his bottom lip. Louis. Right there. So, he didn't want me to go through that, you know, from those notes.

Yeah. I remember he had had several operations, you know, where things were happening. I know at one point, I thought they were taking, you know, some of the pus and things like that out of his lip. I didn't know that they had grafted something on too.
If I understand it right, I think they only grafted something on it.
Did you play with a lot of pressure that way too?
Well, I played with pressure, but not too, I tried not to go too hard cause my lip got sore at times. But, the bottom lip, I used to do most of mine on my top.

I had the trouble on the top lip. But, it's like playing 5 or 6 shows a day, and playing the same tunes in each show, you finally get a little pressure there. You start to use the pressure when you start down to the end of the getting week. You know.
